title: Puzzle 3D UI Freeze Incremental Precompute And Worker Backed Plugins
description: Fix multi-minute UI freezes in puzzle-3d when loading an example or clicking "suggest objects". Root cause part A: Puzzle3dPlayApp::handle_action calls sync_precompute_session -> set_scene unconditionally every action, and set_scene always rebuild_queue()s (wipes brush_cache + FillBuilder + re-enqueues 1000 FillSteps), then drive_precompute grinds 128x32=4096 Monte-Carlo collision task units synchronously; the 120ms suggestionsTick/fillBuildTick loops restart this from zero every tick so it never converges. Fix: make set_scene idempotent (skip rebuild when scene JSON unchanged), invalidate cache on real register_mesh, bound drive_precompute to a single precompute_step(8) per tick, apply same guard to puzzle 5d's drive path. Root cause part B: the React host (framework/core/js/index.ts loadPluginModuleUncached) loads plugin WASM and calls handleAction synchronously on the main thread; port the existing wgpu PluginWorkerClient pattern (framework/renderer/wgpu/js/boot.ts) so plugins run in a Web Worker instead, with no timeout-kill (only a logging watchdog) since long actions must not destroy plugin state.
summary:
Fixed the suggestion-list hover feedback bug reported after the previous close.

Investigated the reported symptoms ("no immediate preview when hovering suggested objects" + "list item doesn't show hover effect") by tracing the full pipeline: `WorldSuggestionMenu`'s row `onMouseEnter` → `dispatch("hoverSuggestion", {index})` → Rust `hoverSuggestion` handler → `runtime.brush_candidate_index` → `world_brush_preview_json` (gated on the host-mirrored `active_tool`, correctly forced to "brush" for the popup's whole lifetime) → `BrushPreviewGhost` render (styled with the existing `palette.highlighted`). Confirmed via code inspection that: candidate index numbering is consistent between the list and the preview lookup (both index into the same `free` candidates list); `ui_scope` defaults to `Full` so every action, including hover, triggers a UI refresh; the hash-based `refreshUi` diffing hashes the full rendered node (which includes `brushPreviewJson`), so a hover-driven change is never silently suppressed; and `collect_mesh_urls` registers fallback meshes for catalog (not-yet-placed) object kinds too, so every listed candidate always has a renderable mesh.

The concrete bug found: `framework/renderer/react/components/world-3d-host.tsx`'s `WorldSuggestionMenu` row markup had **zero** hover styling — plain inline `style={{...}}` with no `className`, no CSS `:hover` rule, and no state-driven highlight. Fixed by applying the app's existing shared `menuListItemClassName` (native CSS `:hover`, the identical treatment used by every other list/menu surface in the app) and adding a `data-selected` attribute reflecting the server-confirmed active candidate index (`interaction.brushCandidateIndex`), so the currently-previewed row is visually marked independent of mouse position too (useful for `cycleBrushCandidate` keyboard navigation, which doesn't involve hover at all).

Verified: `bun nx run @semio-tech/framework-renderer-react:test` — 133/133 passing, no regressions.
